subject: Information Theory
title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography
description: A 60-second lesson on Elliptic Curve Cryptography.

hook.text: RSA needs 3072-bit keys for strong security. Elliptic curves achieve the same strength with just 256 bits.

buildup.text: ECC uses the math of points on curves. Adding points is easy; reversing the operation is extremely hard.

discovery.text: Smaller keys mean faster computation, less bandwidth, and lighter storage—crucial for mobile and IoT devices.

twist.text: Bitcoin, Signal, and TLS 1.3 all use ECC. It replaced RSA as the default for most new systems.

climax.text: The same security with far less data. ECC is the modern standard for public-key cryptography.

punchline.text: Smaller key, same security. Curves beat primes.

quiz.question: What is the main advantage of ECC over RSA?
options: Same security with much smaller keys
